gal_ranger.text: Galloway Forest Park is about three hundred square miles. I've walked a good chunk of it. The rest is walked by sheep, who do not file reports.
If you hear a rustle in the spruce, it's probably a red squirrel, a roe deer or a very quiet hillwalker eating a sandwich.

gal_stargazer.text: Come back at night with no torch. I mean it. After twenty minutes your eyes switch on, and the Milky Way comes out like a spilled sack of sugar.
Fun fact: this park is a Dark Sky Park, and the dark is protected on purpose. It's the only time anyone has been fined for being too bright.

gal_deerwatcher.text: Shh! Oh, hello. The stags are moody this time of year. Keep your voice low and your elbows lower.
There are wild goats in Galloway too, and they've lived on these hills for a very long time. They give a very particular look. A very goat look.

gal_forester.text: Most of the trees here are Sitka spruce, planted for timber in the last century. They grow like they're being timed.
A good forest takes about forty years to grow and about forty minutes to walk through. The maths is on the trees' side.

gal_stag.text: The stag lifts his head, regards you with magnificent boredom, and goes back to grazing.

gal_fawn_a.text: A fawnlet stares at you. It is considering whether you are a snack or a friend.

gal_fawn_b.text: The fawnlet bounces, wobbles, and bounces again. Everything is a new idea.

then.text: The Immortal Memory went down a treat, and nobody fell asleep in the second verse of 'Tam o' Shanter'. A first for the club.
Dumfries is down the road: his house on Burns Street, the Globe Inn where he drank, and the mausoleum at St Michael's. Go when the daffodils are out. He would have.
Both read? Then one question, for the toast. Which of these did Burns write?

options: O my Luve is like a red, red rose
Fifteen men on the dead man's chest
I wandered lonely as a cloud

then.text: 'O my Luve is like a red, red rose, that's newly sprung in June.' 1794, and he said he got the start of it from a country girl's song. The other two are Stevenson and Wordsworth, fine men, wrong country.
The Immortal Memory is yours, then. Here: a facsimile of the Kilmarnock edition, the 1786 one, and a bit of tablet for the walk. Here's tae ye, and a guid New Year when it comes.

else.text: Och, no. That one's Stevenson or Wordsworth, and either of them would be mortified. Have another look at the boards and try me again.
The Dumfries board is read. Now Edinburgh: there is a lectern near the Royal Mile about his winter there in 1786, when the capital made a lion of him and he found it tiring.
The board about Burns in Dumfries is along the path there, by the lochan. Read it first. The Supper is not till you have.
{greeting} Secretary of the Burns Club, for my sins. Burns Night is 25 January, his birthday, and every January I need a new speaker for the Immortal Memory, the toast to the man himself.
The speaker must know two things: how he died, in Dumfries, down the road from here, in 1796, and how he lived, in Edinburgh, for one daft winter ten years before.
There is a board about each. Read the one here in Galloway, then the one in Edinburgh, and come back. I will ask you one question. Get it right and the toast is yours.
